_comment: Hand rules for fields no automatic rule explains (see coverage.md). Keys are '<component>:<path>'. Each names the transform the phase B compiler implements and why inference cannot derive it. Rules the inference did derive are never repeated here.

block:minecraft:embedded_visual:material.why: The value is a whole minecraft:material_instances object, sent inline with per-face {texture, render_method, tint_method, ambient_occlusion, face_dimming, isotropic, alpha_masked_tint}. Setting it also fills in the sibling geometry description's defaults (bone_visibility, culling, ...), so per-field correlation cannot separate the two. Reuse the material_instances field rules per face.

block:minecraft:item_visual:material_ins.why: Sent as materialInstancesDescription in the minecraft:material_instances wire shape: face aliases go to 'mappings', faces to 'materials', and face_dimming/isotropic are packed into 'packed_bools' (bit 0 face_dimming, bit 1 isotropic, bit 2 always set). The bit packing combines two JSON fields into one leaf, which single-field variation cannot fit.

block:minecraft:placement_filter:conditi.why: Descriptor states become a list of {state, type, value} with the value as the state's int/string/byte. The type depends on the state's definition in the block registry, not on the JSON value. A state the named block does not have makes BDS drop the descriptor, so arbitrary sample state names give no mapping.

item:minecraft:block_placer:use_on[].sta.why: Same block descriptor as placement_filter: state values are resolved against the named block (e.g. pillar_axis 'y' -> 0). Unknown states drop the entry, so the mapping depends on registry data, not on the JSON alone.

item:minecraft:digger:destroy_speeds[].b.why: Same block descriptor resolution; the capture's variants with sample state names removed the whole destroy_speeds entry.

item:minecraft:entity_placer:use_on[].st.why: Same block descriptor resolution as block_placer.use_on.

item:minecraft:entity_placer:dispense_on.why: Same block descriptor resolution as block_placer.use_on.

block:permutations:[].components.why: A permutation's components use each block component's own wire rules, under permutations[].components. A permutation with no components is not sent at all, which takes its condition leaf with it. Compile each nested component with its component mapping and drop empty permutations.

item:minecraft:food:using_converts_to.why: The docs type it as a string or keyed set of strings; BDS takes a string or {name}, sends {name: <item>} for a known item and {} otherwise. The output depends on whether the item exists, which no rule over the JSON value captures.

item:minecraft:hover_text_color:value.why: The component keeps the color name; item_properties.hover_text_color gets the formatting code (red -> §c, dark_purple -> §5) and is left out for unknown names. The docs give no enum for the field, so a value table cannot be generalized. Implement it with Bedrock's text color table. With no value, BDS sends the component with an empty value.

block:minecraft:collision_box:[].why: Each box's min/max leaves depend on both origin and size (min = origin + (8, 0, 8), max = min + size; BDS orders min and max per axis), so single-field variation fits spurious linear rules to each and they conflict on every leaf.

block:minecraft:geometry:.why: BDS rejected every variant's companions (status untestable), so no rule was inferred. The wire shape is known from every material_instances variant, which carries a geometry: {identifier, bone_visibility, culling, culling_layer, culling_shape, uv_lock, ignoreGeometryForIsSolid, isV1Fullblock, needsLegacyTopRotation, useBlockTypeLightAbsorption}; item_visual sends the same shape as geometryDescription.

block:minecraft:material_instances:.why: face_dimming and isotropic are packed into one byte (packed_bools: bit 0 face_dimming, bit 1 isotropic, bit 2 always set), so each field's table only fits with the other at its default; face aliases go to mappings, faces to materials. Inference cannot combine two fields into one leaf.

item:minecraft:repairable:repair_items.why: Each entry's items become [{name}] (names as written, not namespaced) next to repair_amount, a float for numbers and a string for Molang. The two JSON types of repair_amount land on the same leaf with different NBT types, which no single rule fits.

block:minecraft:embedded_visual:geometry.why: The same geometry description as minecraft:geometry, inline. BDS rejected every embedded_visual variant of the capture, so this shape is the documented one with the wire keys of minecraft:geometry (unverified).

block:minecraft:transformation:rotation.why: Rotation is sent as RX/RY/RZ in quarter turns (degrees / 90). Only multiples of 90 are accepted, and the variant values 90/180/270 vary all three axes at once, so per-axis rules could not be fitted.

block:minecraft:placement_filter:conditi.why: A list of faces becomes a byte bit set (down 1, up 2, north 4, south 8, west 16, east 32; 63 for the default all). Every list variant was rejected by BDS, so no bitset rule could be fitted; the encoding is the one liquid_detection and vanilla data show.

block:minecraft:liquid_detection:detecti.why: Same face bit set as placement_filter allowed_faces (stopsLiquidFromDirection); BDS rejected every list variant, so only the empty default (0) was observed.

block:minecraft:redstone_producer:connec.why: Sent as the list of face names, all six by default. BDS rejected every varied list, so only the default list was observed, which inference cannot turn into a rule (its per-index leaves differ).

block:minecraft:connection_rule:enabled_.why: Same as redstone_producer connected_faces: the list of directions, default [south, north, east, west].

block:trait:minecraft:placement_directio.why: enabled_states becomes one byte per state the trait can enable (cardinal_direction, corner_and_cardinal_direction, facing_direction, sixteen_way_rotation), 1 if listed. Inference fitted a table on the first element and could not see the others.

item:minecraft:icon:.why: The icon lives only in item_properties.minecraft:icon as {textures: {default: <texture>}}; the string form and textures map variants both write that compound, but the documented texture field is unknown to BDS and textures was dropped (no varied value).

item:minecraft:dyeable:default_color.why: default_color is a hex string or [r, g, b] and is sent as a list of three ints, white [255, 255, 255] by default; inference dropped the field because the varied values all fell back to white or were rejected.

block:minecraft:destructible_by_mining:.why: value is seconds_to_destroy (0 by default, -1 for the false form), item_specific_speeds is only sent when not empty, in the legacy {Name, Aux} item descriptor shape. Single field variation fitted count/table rules for value that conflict.

block:minecraft:selection_box:.why: Every origin variant was rejected (BDS validates the box against the block bounds), so origin has no rule; the wire always carries enabled, origin and size, the full cube when the false form disables selection.

item:minecraft:use_animation:value.why: item_properties.use_animation numbers the animation (eat 1, spear 6, ...). The docs give no enum for value, so the inference only saw the two samples and fitted a constant; the numbering is Bedrock's UseAnimation enum.
